agents/agent-studio:
Agent Studio is the chat-first way to use a saved agent.
The chat is the main surface, and the canvas folds into a slim strip you can reopen.

## One sandbox per chat

A chat gets one warm sandbox, and follow-ups reuse it.
A paused sandbox is woken with its files.
Only a destroyed sandbox is replaced, and the chat says so.

## Honest status and errors

The status line shows what is happening: starting the sandbox, starting the agent, thinking.
A failed message shows the platform's own message, its code, and one hint, shown once on the turn.

## The workspace panel

A workspace panel sits beside the chat, with the same tabs as Optimal:

- Preview
- Files
- Code
- Terminal
- Machine
- Logs

It opens on the chat's first activity and shows the chat's own sandbox.

## A clean conversation

Harness wording such as Overdrive warnings and the stdin banner never reaches the chat.
Overdrive is one quiet chip beside the composer with a tooltip.
Tool rows stay inside the chat: a long argument can no longer widen it, and commands, arguments, and JSON output are readable.

Past chats are kept per agent in both Agent Studio and the agent page.

## Related

- [Chat with an agent on a machine](/docs/agents/chat-on-a-machine): the chat on a computer or sandbox page.
- [Configure an agent](/docs/guides/configure-agent): instructions, model, tools, and permissions.
agents/chat-on-a-machine:
Opening a computer, or the Agent section of a sandbox, opens one chat bound to that machine.
The workspace panel sits beside it.

## Pick the brain in the chat

Before the first message you choose what powers the chat:

- **Optimal** runs a machine-bound chat on wallet credits.
- **A harness** runs on your own account: Claude Code, Codex, OSA, pi, OpenCode, Prime Agent, Kimi Code, or Mistral Vibe.
- **A saved agent** runs with its own instructions, tools, and permissions.

The chat is bound to the machine you opened, so there is no "where should you build?" step.

The brain is remembered per person, per workspace, and per machine.
It never changes the brain you picked on the [Optimal](/docs/optimal) page.

## While it works

- Switching the brain stops the run, keeps the old thread above a divider, and starts a new thread.
- A Connect card opens when your account is not connected.
- Approvals appear inline, and you can approve or deny.
- **Stop** cancels the run.
- **Take over** hands control to you, and **Hand back** returns it.

## The panel follows the machine

The workspace panel opens on Desktop for a computer and on Terminal for a sandbox, then Preview once a URL exists.
It restores the layout you had on the Optimal page when you leave.

A machine that belongs to another workspace never gets a chat, a chat id, or a run.

## Related

- [Agent Studio](/docs/agents/agent-studio): the chat-first agent workspace.
- [Build on your machines](/docs/optimal/machines): the panel and its tabs.
agents/confinement:
An agent runs inside its machine and stays there.
It cannot use MIOSA's own platform key to reach the rest of the platform.

## The platform key is blanked

Every sandbox boots with a platform key and its ids in the environment, so a plain command can call MIOSA.

Harness runs do not get it.
When MIOSA starts a harness, it blanks the platform key and the ids at launch, and unsets them in the run script.
So Claude Code, Codex, OSA, pi, OpenCode, Prime Agent, Kimi Code, Mistral Vibe, and Hermes Agent cannot borrow MIOSA's key.

## Grant a scoped key with an Environment

When you want an agent to reach MIOSA on purpose, an [Environment](/docs/cli/environments) can grant it a scoped machine key.
That key is bound to the machine, not to your account.

## What is kept

- A value the run itself supplies is kept.
- Environment grants are not touched.

## Related

- [Isolation and permissions](/docs/optimal/isolation): what a hosted chat can touch.
- [Runtime environment](/docs/guides/runtime-env): variables by scope and target.
agents/harnesses:
A harness is a coding agent MIOSA runs on a machine, on your own account.
MIOSA never falls back to its own keys.

## The harnesses

| Harness | `runner` |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude-code` |
| Codex | `codex` |
| OSA | `osa` |
| pi | `pi` |
| OpenCode | `opencode` |
| Prime Agent | `prime` |
| Kimi Code | `kimi` |
| Mistral Vibe | `mistral` |
| Hermes Agent | `hermes` |

There is also `custom` for a gateway model, which runs on MIOSA's AI Gateway.

## How MIOSA gets them ready

Runs are fast because a machine rarely installs anything at run time.

| Ready | Harnesses |
|---|---|
| Prebaked in the machine image | Claude Code, Codex, OSA |
| Installed on first use | pi, OpenCode, Prime Agent, Kimi Code, Mistral Vibe |
| Add-on, installed at create | Hermes Agent |

Hermes Agent is a large install, about 2.5 GB, so it is added at create and cached per host.

## Which account powers which harness

A Connection you make once is reused by every harness that accepts it.
Connect a ChatGPT plan once, and Codex, pi, OpenCode, Prime Agent, and Hermes Agent all use it.

| Harness | Plans | API keys |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | Claude plan | Anthropic, OpenRouter, DeepSeek; Amazon Bedrock |
| Codex | ChatGPT plan | OpenAI, DeepSeek; Amazon Bedrock |
| OSA | | Ollama Cloud; Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter |
| pi | Claude plan, ChatGPT plan, Mistral Vibe key | Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Mistral, LLM Gateway |
| OpenCode | ChatGPT plan, Mistral Vibe key | Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Mistral, LLM Gateway |
| Prime Agent | Claude plan, ChatGPT plan, Mistral Vibe key | Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Mistral, LLM Gateway |
| Kimi Code | Kimi Code plan | Moonshot |
| Mistral Vibe | Mistral Vibe key | Mistral |
| Hermes Agent | ChatGPT plan, Claude plan (Max with extra usage) | Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter |

Two caveats to know:

- **OpenCode cannot use a Claude plan.** Anthropic does not allow it, and OpenCode removed the plugins that did it.
- **Hermes Agent on a Claude plan needs a Claude Max plan with extra usage credits.** A Claude Pro plan is refused.

## Hermes Agent

Hermes Agent is a first-class runner in the run API: send `runner: "hermes"` to `POST /api/v1/runs`.
It is not in the CLI `--harness` list yet, so use the API or the console until it is.

MIOSA runs the platform's pinned Hermes version, and never installs a newer one.
A Hermes run without an account returns `OWN_CREDENTIALS_REQUIRED`, the same as any other harness.

## The harness list as an API

`GET /api/v1/agents/harnesses` returns each harness with:

- `supported_auth`: the accounts that can power it, in the order the run path tries them.
  Each has `id`, `label`, `kind`, `vendor`, `injection`, `model`, `source`, and `note`.
- `also_supports`: what the agent's own CLI takes that MIOSA does not connect yet.
- `unsupported_auth`: what a person may expect to work but the vendor refuses, with `reason` and `source`.

Each model carries `served_by`, the account ids that can run it.

Refresh tokens never reach a machine.
The control plane is the single refresh owner, and hands the machine a short-lived access token that outlives the run.
